title: Spiral galaxy NGC 4945
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 4945 and surrounding sky, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This wide field is centered on the spiral galaxy NGC 4945. Around it, faint, slightly red patches are much more distant galaxies, and most of the point-like sources are stars in our own Milky Way. A good number of the points near NGC 4945, though, are globular clusters belonging to the galaxy itself.

Globular clusters are dense, ball-shaped groups of old stars that orbit galaxies. Picking them out among foreground stars requires a sharp image, and this one resolves about 1 arcsecond, which corresponds to roughly 62 light-years at the galaxy's distance, given here as 13 million light-years.

The photo was made with the Wide-Field-Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla, during the camera's early testing phase. It was assembled from 14 CCD frames, together recording more than 70 x 10 9 photons, and it covers a patch of sky 32 by 32 arcminutes.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide-Field-Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope. A narrow red filter is shown in red, a blue filter in green, and an ultraviolet filter in blue.
understand.eye: The colors are shifted from their real hues, and part of the data is ultraviolet light, which the eye cannot see.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The red filter was very narrow, and because of how fast NGC 4945 is moving away from us, it does not capture the galaxy's glowing hydrogen emission. Each frame recorded 67,076,064 pixels.
alt: A wide field of stars around a spiral galaxy, with faint reddish distant galaxies scattered through the frame.
